The initiative offers 20 per cent equity loans for buyers with small deposits.
Conservatives warned the policy could increase buyer debt and drive up house prices.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced the Your First Home scheme to assist first-time buyers in England. The initiative offers a 20 per cent equity loan for new-build properties to buyers providing a 2.5 per cent deposit. Income, deposit, and property price caps will apply. Additionally, the government announced plans to make it easier for local councils to take over long-term empty homes and convert them into housing.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Supporters argue the policy helps young buyers lacking family financial support, while giving housebuilders confidence to build. However, Conservative critics warn that the scheme risks driving up property prices and increasing buyer debt burdens. Reports differ on announcement details: one outlet notes John Healey will formally announce the programme in the budget, while another attributes housing policy unveils to Angela Rayner.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Further details on how the equity loan scheme operates are expected in the upcoming Budget, with registration targeted to open by the end of 2026.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Following late-night legal hearings in Belfast, judges cleared an Orange Order parade along Garvaghy Road in Portadown. An earlier injunction temporarily suspending the march was overturned, upholding the Parades Commission's approval. The commission imposed restrictions, though reports varied slightly on the specifics, noting either an departure no later than 08:00 with no bands or an 8am start limited to 35 participants.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The Drumcree parade had not taken place for nearly 30 years following serious sectarian disorder in the 1990s. Nationalist leaders, including First Minister Michelle O'Neill, condemned the decision to permit the march, while Democratic Unionist MP Carla Lockhart insisted residents have nothing to fear.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Broadcaster and campaigner Dame Esther Rantzen has died aged 86. Her family confirmed her death, paying tribute to her legacy of compassion. Rantzen, who was diagnosed with stage four lung cancer in 2023, became a prominent campaigner for assisted dying. She had planned to end her life at the Swiss clinic Dignitas but became too physically frail to make the journey.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rantzen was a pioneering television presenter, hosting the BBC's popular consumer show That's Life! for 21 years. She used her platform to launch Childline in 1986, a helpline for children experiencing abuse. In 2010, she established the Silver Line to support older people. sections.text: A new wave of heavy rain and landslides has killed about 30 people in Nepal. Over 1,900 families have been affected, with homes, roads and bridges damaged or swept away. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: At least 32 child deaths occurred since May in remote villages in Balaghat district, Madhya Pradesh. Officials attribute the fatalities mainly to measles and malaria, worsened by malnutrition and delayed medical care. Many families relied on faith healers or attributed illnesses to a disease goddess.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The deaths highlight deep vulnerabilities among the Baiga, a particularly vulnerable tribal group. Remote terrain, poor transport, and widespread malnutrition severely limit access to basic healthcare and public services.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Health workers conducted door-to-door screenings and deployed mobile medical units to treat thousands of patients. Authorities launched an emergency vaccination campaign for children under 15, and the outbreak has now subsided.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Governor Gavin Newsom signed Assembly bill 1267, prohibiting minors from receiving a marriage licence or entering a domestic partnership. The law contains no exceptions. Previously, children of any age could marry with parental consent and judicial approval.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: California is the 18th state to ban child marriage since 2018, leaving it legal in 32 states. The advocacy group Unchained At Last reported that about 9,000 children—predominantly girls—were wed annually in California, mostly to adult men. Survivors highlighted that minors could not legally divorce, leaving them vulnerable to abuse.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: A survivor noted that minors cannot marry in California after 1 January 2027. Activists, including survivor Courtney Stodden, pledged to continue campaigning until child marriage is banned across all 50 US states.

Barrister Paul Greaney KC said the hotel chain's security policies were unfit for purpose.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In December 2022, a man obtained a key to a guest's room at a Maidenhead Travelodge and sexually assaulted her. An independent review by Paul Greaney KC found the chain failed the victim "at every stage", including offering her an "insulting" £30 refund.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The review found Travelodge's security policies were unfit for purpose. Despite recent changes, guests remain at risk, with room intrusions reported at nearly one in ten Travelodge hotels this summer.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Travelodge has apologised and established a board committee to implement the review's 38 recommendations. These include introducing staff body cameras, consistent CCTV, and stricter key security checks.

fivew: An independent review led by barrister Paul Greaney KC.

gist: Ukraine continues striking Russian oil refineries despite Donald Trump urging a halt.
The strikes reduce Russian refining capacity and contribute to rising US diesel prices.
Kyiv argues it must target infrastructure while Russia bombards Ukrainian cities.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ukraine struck an oil facility in Russia’s Samara region, a Russian vessel in the Black Sea, and a drone site in Oryol. Donald Trump urged Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt refinery attacks, blaming them for global diesel shortages and rising US fuel prices.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The attacks have knocked out over 45% of Russia’s refining capacity. However, they also tighten global diesel supplies and increase cost of living pressures in the US ahead of midterm elections, though analysts cite other market disruptions too.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Kyiv is unlikely to stop targeting Russian oil infrastructure while Moscow continues its daily attacks. Russia has extended its diesel export ban until the end of October.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Neighbouring farmers Derek Gow and Derek Banbury clashed over land use in Devon. Banbury maintained traditional dairy and crop farming, while Gow engaged in rewilding his land by introducing wild boar and championing beavers. Wild boar breached fencing and fed on sheep, annoying neighbours, though a coexistence developed between the two men.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The documentary explores debates around environmental damage, agriculture and the countryside through engaging characters with opposing points of view, highlighting issues such as declining insect populations and endangered traditional farming.

timeline.text: Drumcree policing operation has cost £3m so far, says Boutcher

gist: The Drumcree policing operation has cost approximately £3m so far, says Jon Boutcher.
Police will not force an Orange Order march through a hostile crowd, Boutcher stated.
A code-of-conduct investigation has been launched into Policing Board member Deirdre Hargey.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Chief Constable Jon Boutcher announced that the Drumcree parading dispute's policing operation has cost about £3m. The stand-off began on Sunday over a proposed Orange Order parade in Portadown, opposed by Garvaghy Road nationalist residents. Although the Parades Commission ruled the march could lawfully proceed, police have not forced it through due to an unlawful protest.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Boutcher warned that forcing the march could have "catastrophic" consequences. The Drumcree dispute, which began in the mid-1990s, previously caused severe violence, nearly derailing the peace process. Additionally, the Policing Board is investigating member Deirdre Hargey of Sinn Féin after she was pictured at the protest.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Boutcher is allowing space for negotiations. A thorough police investigation into the protest is underway, and a fresh legal challenge by the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition will be heard on Friday.

sections.text: Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo, his wife Lucy Muteke, and four others died when their helicopter crashed in the Marondera rural area on Wednesday evening. The group was travelling from Gandami, where they were building a home, when the aircraft came down.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Chivayo, known as "Sir Wicknell", was a prominent figure with close ties to several African presidents, including Zimbabwe's Emmerson Mnangagwa and Kenya's William Ruto. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The US supreme court agreed to hear a challenge to the Trump administration's practice of indefinite detention for undocumented immigrants awaiting deportation. The administration reinterpreted a longstanding policy last year, denying bond hearings to migrants who entered the country illegally. The challenge was brought by Ricardo Aparecido Barbosa da Cunha, a Brazilian citizen living in the US who was denied a bond hearing after being arrested by ICE agents.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The sustainable farming incentive opened, and an application was submitted to become organic, but funding ran out within hours. Meanwhile, the farm has been under a bovine tuberculosis shutdown since June, complicating cattle sales. During preparations for a new test, 67 cows were brought home from the fells, and one calved on the hillside. Following testing, an inconclusive reactor with a 3mm lump was found, resulting in a continued shutdown.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The quick exhaustion of government funding leaves farmers uncertain about business survival, highlighting a need for more financial support. Additionally, ongoing bovine tuberculosis restrictions prevent the sale of breeding cows except direct to slaughter, creating significant financial impact and sleepless nights for the farmer.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara and expelled ten Eritrean diplomats, accusing them of threatening national security. Eritrea responded by severing all diplomatic ties. sections.text: The breakdown in relations between the former allies raises fears of a wider regional conflict. It follows the collapse of the 2022 peace agreement, threatening thousands of displaced people, humanitarian operations, and regional stability.

sections.text: The Court of Appeal quashed Julie Ann McIlwaine's murder conviction. She had stabbed her abusive partner, James Joseph Crossley, while he slept in March 2022. The court found that the trial judge misdirected the jury regarding her loss-of-control defence.

gist: Intensified Russian strikes are tearing Kyiv apart, warns mayor Vitali Klitschko.
Attacks hit bridges, energy infrastructure and residential areas, causing major disruptions.
President Zelenskyy says Putin ordered commanders to abandon the rules of war.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Russian forces launched intensified drone and missile strikes against Kyiv, hitting the Pivdennyi bridge, a school, a hospital, datacentres and energy facilities. The attacks have suspended bridge traffic, cut power and water in several neighbourhoods, and caused residential casualties.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The escalation reshapes everyday life in a capital of three million people, bringing winter hardships early and straining defence systems as Russia targets critical infrastructure and seeks to create a humanitarian crisis.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Kyiv is racing to fast-track new interceptor drones, though deploying them at scale could take weeks or months. Meanwhile, western diplomats are drawing up contingency plans to relocate embassies if Russia targets foreign missions.

fivew: Russian and Ukrainian forces and residents.
Intensified Russian missile and drone strikes hit Kyiv.
Russia aims to sow panic and destroy infrastructure, while Putin claimed attacks on economic targets respond to Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries.

timeline.text: ‘Just like my big brothers’: boy with cerebral palsy passes GCSEs with eye-tracking technology

gist: Patrick McCabe, a 16-year-old with cerebral palsy, passed his GCSEs using eye-tracking technology.
He completed his exams over four months and has now started studying for his A-levels.
His story highlights the challenges and funding issues faced by students with special educational needs.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Patrick McCabe used eye-tracking technology to complete his GCSE exams over four months. Despite facing exhaustion and communication barriers, he passed all seven exams and started studying for his A-levels in French, business, and media studies at Fallibroome Academy.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Patrick's success highlights the potential of inclusive education, but also exposes significant hurdles. His family and school had to battle exam boards for a fair chance, revealing that current exams are not fully accessible and that schools lack sufficient funding and vital expertise.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Patrick has transitioned to sixth form wearing a smart blue suit and plans to study media at university after completing his A-levels, with ambitions to enter the media industry.

sections.text: The setup allows residents to stay cool during extreme heat while helping the local power grid manage electricity demand. It turns residential units into a virtual power plant, providing a business model that shares financial benefits with consumers.

timeline.text: 'Cult' priest guilty of rape and assault of women

gist: Former priest Chris Brain was found guilty of raping a woman.
Brain was convicted of multiple sexual offences against congregation members.
Victims waited decades for justice as church leaders faced scrutiny.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Chris Brain, a former priest who led the Nine O'Clock Service in Sheffield, was found guilty of raping a congregation member and four counts of indecent assault. This follows convictions for 17 indecent assaults at a previous trial. Jurors heard the group functioned as a cult where members were isolated and dependent on Brain, who abused his position to commit numerous sexual offences.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The verdicts bring accountability for 22 offences against 13 women. Victims and lawyers highlighted institutional failures by the Church of England, stating leaders ignored warning signs, protected Brain, and failed in their duty of care over decades.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Brain is in custody awaiting a sentencing hearing likely to take two days, where victims will deliver impact statements. An independent safeguarding review into the Diocese of Sheffield's response continues, alongside civil action against the Church of England.

gist: Researchers detected a tantalizing hint of dark matter using the LUX-ZEPLIN detector.
Physicists observed quantum entanglement in pairs of Z bosons at the Large Hadron Collider.
Engineers created a Martian building material from rocks, gelatin, and yeast.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Scientists reported several recent discoveries, including a possible dark matter signal at the LUX-ZEPLIN detector in South Dakota and quantum entanglement in Z bosons at the Large Hadron Collider. Additionally, engineers developed a living 3D-printable building material for Mars using yeast and gelatin, archaeologists found evidence of Ice Age humans chewing betel nuts 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, and a historian uncovered a 1666 description of a telescope attributed to Galileo. Finally, research revealed that 19th-century cosmoramas were used to market real estate.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: These findings advance several fields. The dark matter signal, if confirmed, could help physicists understand the universe, while observing high-energy entanglement aids quantum research. The yeast mixture offers a cost-effective, low-energy housing solution for colonizing Mars. The dental evidence provides insight into early human habits and health, and the historical texts shed new light on Galileo's scientific instruments and early real estate marketing methods.

fivew: Researchers highlighted several cool science stories, including potential dark matter signals, particle entanglement, Martian building materials, ancient psychoactive use, and historical telescope descriptions.
Various global locations including South Dakota, Japan, Italy, Indonesia, and Ireland.

timeline.text: Miami-inspired London house features on Grand Designs

gist: A pair of pale-pink London homes inspired by Miami recently featured on television.
Architect Peter Morris spent roughly ten years developing the semi-detached properties.
The buildings showcase sweeping arches and duck-egg blue metalwork details.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Two pale-pink homes called The Cloud House finished construction in Gospel Oak, north London. Designed by architect Peter Morris over ten years, the semi-detached properties share an exterior look featuring sweeping arches and duck-egg blue metalwork, and appeared on Channel 4's Grand Designs.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The project gained public attention through its feature on a popular television series, showcasing a unique design inspired by Miami and a local church.

fivew: A pair of pale-pink homes appeared on television.
The project was inspired by a local church and architecture from another city.

A commission described the financial accounts as a concerted campaign to falsify.
The club has until Friday to mount an appeal against the guilty verdicts.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester City spent 1.2 billion pounds on transfers and falsified financial accounts by adding 830 million pounds.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Without the extra funds, the club could not have signed players of the same quantity and quality, raising questions about past success.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: City have until Friday to appeal. If unsuccessful, they will face punishment, and the future consequences remain uncertain.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Portugal coach Jorge Jesus denied reports of a rift with captain Cristiano Ronaldo after the forward headed straight to the changing rooms following a win over Norway. Jesus explained that no player is happy about not coming on as a substitute. Jesus also dismissed claims that Ronaldo had refused to train, stating the player needed individual exercises.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Ronaldo did not feature in the match against Norway and Jesus confirmed that AC Milan striker Goncalo Ramos will again be preferred for the upcoming fixture against Denmark.

timeline.text: England call up Crane and rest Archer for Pakistan series

gist: Mason Crane is recalled to England's squad for the Pakistan tri-series.
Jofra Archer is rested while Jos Buttler is out injured.
Uncapped pair James Coles and Henry Crocombe are included.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Mason Crane has been recalled for England's upcoming one-day international tri-series in Pakistan. Sam Curran and Adil Rashid return from injuries, while uncapped players James Coles and Henry Crocombe join the squad. Jofra Archer is rested, and Jos Buttler misses out due to a hamstring injury.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The series forms part of England's white-ball schedule as they build up to the 50-over World Cup. Crane also has an opportunity to push his case to be England's number one spinner in Test cricket.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: England will play in the tri-series in Pakistan, which also involves Sri Lanka, ahead of further fixtures in Australia and South Africa.

fivew: England are building up to the 50-over World Cup and rotating their squad and coaching staff.
